text:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: prod alert -> cont-batch service 'inference-pool-prod-7' showing sudden throughput stallback + KV-cache growth. 5xxs up ~4x, P95 latency jumping. Paging on-call. https://ops.redwood.example/incidents/1745555555

sara: i'm on it — seeing queueing at router, requests piling in backlog. microbatch size distribution shifted: median 8 -> 28, spikes to 64. suspect continuous-batching policy misfired under high concurrency.

dan: metrics show kvcache entries +3x in last 10m, eviction rate spiking and OOM-driven evictions. retention window blown out.

sara: grabbing logs from node-07:```
[2026-03-16T08:52:12Z] batch_manager: admitted 1024 reqs -> microbatch size 64
[2026-03-16T08:52:13Z] kvcache: items=12.8M, evict/sec=1240, reclaim=FAIL
[2026-03-16T08:52:14Z] runtime: async-queue-length=324, tail-latency=9.4s
```

mitra: quick mitigation idea: cap microbatch size and reduce prefetch aggressiveness. Suggested hotfix: set continuous_batch.max_microbatch=12 and prefetch.adaptive_alpha=0.2 for prod pool. That should limit KV blowout and lower per-request latency.

sara: preparing hotpatch canary on pool nodes node-07a/node-07b. will do rolling config update via orchestrator. command: ``curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $OP' https://controlplane/api/v1/pools/prod-7/config -d '{"continuous_batch.max_microbatch":12, "prefetch.adaptive_alpha":0.2}'``

infra-bot: deploy started to canary group (node-07a,node-07b). build 2026.03.16-hotfix-1745.

infra-bot: canary deploy succeeded in 60s.

mitra: watching metrics — canary shows drop in median microbatch -> 10, eviction rate down 70%, P95 latency down ~35%. good signal.

lee: i propose enabling short-term route-level throttles for public endpoints to keep system stable while we push rollout. can we set route throttle to 50r/s for /v1/generate?

sara: applied route throttle via config lambda. command: ``rbctl routes update --route /v1/generate --limit 50`` -> took effect. latency improved further, backlog draining.

olivia: customer-impact note: CS flagged two high-tier customers saw 5-10s tail latencies and some request failures between 08:50-09:05 UTC. i've informed them and logged incident for follow-up.

dan: rolling to remaining nodes now (8/12 nodes patched). rolling update in progress, will monitor for jitter re-emergence.

sara: update: after full rollout, average microbatch back to 8-12, kvcache stable, overall 5xxs returned to baseline. still seeing occasional jitter bursts correlated with short spikes in concurrency.

mitra: root suspected: adaptive prefetch heuristic overshot under sudden concurrency surge; continuous-batching allowed large microbatches which amplified KV-cache pressure and caused eviction storms -> perf cliff.

dan: follow-ups: 1) revert adaptive prefetch tuning into safer default values; 2) add smoothing to microbatch increments (max delta per second); 3) add a short-circuit fallback: if eviction rate > X then force microbatch cap and disable prefetch for 30s; 4) add synthetic canary test for concurrency ramp to detect heuristic overshoot.

lee: created a rollout ticket and a config-change RFC: RFC-2026-CB-PREFETCH (link).

olivia: CS summary posted to incident page and customers notified with mitigation timeline.

mitra: handing over monitoring to next oncall (mitra takes night watch) — i'll keep an eye for next 2 hours and run extra health checks every 5m. if eviction/sec > 200 trigger automated rollback.

sara: handing off details: hotfix patch 2026.03.16-hotfix-1745; route throttle id rt-1745; affected pool prod-7; customer impact logged for acct:acme-123 and acct:omega-77.

dan: thanks team. please add any logs + dashboards to the postmortem. i'll open a postmortem ticket and assign to eng-ml + eng-runtime for deeper fix. :thumbsup:

oncall-bot: Pager note recorded, incident status -> mitigated. Postmortem pending.
